nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong high-desert sun drives plant growth, but it also dries the soil in a park that gets only about 10 inches of rain a year.

nodes.name: Summer monsoon rain
nodes.desc: About 42 percent of the park's scarce rain falls from July to September, triggering the main burst of grass and wildflower growth.

nodes.name: Badland and clay soils
nodes.desc: Erodible clay soils of the Painted Desert hold little water and nutrients, so the grassland on better soils is a prized, slow-recovering resource.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to thin desert soil.

nodes.name: Blue grama
nodes.desc: A short bunchgrass that dominates the desert grassland. Wikipedia lists blue grama among the common grasses of the park.

nodes.name: Four-wing saltbush
nodes.desc: A tough, salt-tolerant shrub well recorded near the park. Its leaves and seeds feed many grazers and browsers.

nodes.name: Cliff prickly-pear
nodes.desc: A low, spiny cactus of the park's shrub steppe. Pronghorn diet studies list cacti as a notable food.

nodes.name: Rough harvester ant
nodes.desc: A seed-collecting ant that stores seeds in underground nests. It is a common insect of the park's dry grassland.

nodes.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A nocturnal desert rodent that feeds mainly on seeds and can live without drinking water.

nodes.name: Gunnison's prairie dog
nodes.desc: Lives in colonies and eats mostly grasses and herbs. Its burrowing loosens soil and creates habitat, and many predators hunt it.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: A long-eared hare of open desert grassland that eats grasses and shrubs. Prey for nearly every predator here.

nodes.name: Pronghorn
nodes.desc: The fastest land mammal in North America. It eats forbs, shrubs, cacti and grasses, and is hunted by coyotes, bobcats and golden eagles.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and herbs. Wikipedia notes it visits the park's Painted Desert rim.

nodes.name: Collared lizard
nodes.desc: The most common large lizard in the park. It hunts insects and smaller lizards from rocks.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor common in the park. It eats rodents, rabbits and birds.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird near the park. An omnivore that scavenges carrion and takes small prey.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that locates carcasses by sight and smell and cleans up dead animals across the grassland.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A hawk that hunts rabbits, prairie dogs, rodents, reptiles and birds from perches over open ground.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: The park's top mammal predator. It hunts rabbits, rodents and pronghorn, and also scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A stealthy cat that hunts rabbits, rodents and birds, and sometimes larger prey such as pronghorn.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: The park's largest bird, with a wingspan up to about 7 feet. It hunts rabbits, prairie dogs and sometimes pronghorn.
